title: Design and performance comparison of Vernier and conventional PM synchronous wind generators

source.citation: P. M. Tlali, R.-J. Wang, S. Gerber, C. D. Botha, M. J. Kamper, IEEE Transactions on Industry Applications 56(3), 2020, pp. 2570-2579

machine.topology: outer-rotor surface-PM Vernier machine: open-shoe stator teeth modulate the 66-pole rotor field for a 6-pole overlapping double-layer winding (Ns = Q = pr + ps)
machine.symmetry: The whole cross-section is modelled (gcd(36, 66) = 6 would allow a 60 degree antiperiodic sector). A rotor pole pitch negates every linkage (half-wave symmetry at no load); at balanced load currents the torque repeats every sixth of an electrical period (1.818 degrees).

components_map.part: stator laminations: parallel teeth with tapered shoes, open slots closed at the shoe roots, two radial coil layers
components_map.component: slotted_stator (tapered shoes, shoe-root closure and layer divider, new)

components_map.part: overlapping double-layer winding, coils pitched 5 of 6 slots
66 radially magnetized arc magnets on an outer rotor yoke
rotor yoke and outer boundary, stator bore and hub
sliding band in the 1.5 mm gap, turning the stator side for an outer rotor

slots.note: PMSM 48, PMVM 36; the slots' teeth are the PMVM's modulators (Ns = Q, Section III).

rotor_pole_pairs.note: Table IV: 66 rotor poles; Ns = pr + ps (eq. (1)).

outer_diameter_mm.note: The rotor's outer diameter (Fig. 3(a): Dout/2 on the rotor yoke).

inner_diameter_mm.note: The stator yoke's inner diameter (Fig. 3(b): Di/2).

rotor_yoke_mm.note: Fig. 6(a): 13.56 mm (rotor yoke inner surface at 202.94 mm).

magnet_span_ratio.note: theta_pm_s / theta_pm_p with theta_pm_p = pi/pr (eq. (6)); Fig. 6(a): 4.795 of 5.4545 degrees, 0.879.

stator_yoke_table_mm.note: Recorded, not used: with the other radial dimensions and Di it cannot hold (60.56 against 60 mm); Fig. 6(a) shows 13.14 mm (slot bottoms at 169.598, bore 156.455), and the build takes the yoke as what Di leaves (13.04 mm). Control stator-yoke-13p6 moves the bore in to give 13.6 mm.

slot_angle_ratio.note: theta_s / theta_sp (eq. (6)), theta_s measured at the slot bottom (Fig. 3(b)): the teeth are parallel-sided (Fig. 6(a): half-widths 3.839-3.845 mm from the slot bottom to the shoes), 2.6 degrees wide at the slot bottom.

slot_opening_ratio.note: theta_so / theta_s (eq. (6)). Read with theta_s taken at the tip radius between the tooth sides extended, the ratio gives tip arcs of 2 x 1.8151 degrees; Fig. 6(a) shows 2 x 1.8168 (five teeth, 1.8162-1.8172). The literal reading (theta_s at the slot bottom, 7.4 degrees) gives 6.068 degrees of opening against the drawn 6.367: control opening-literal.

current_density_bound_A_per_mm2.note: The optimization's constraint J <= 5 A/mm2 (Section IV), recorded; not the operating point (see gaps).

winding_loss_W.note: The PMVM's FEA winding loss at rated conditions.

copper_mass_kg.note: Active winding including the end windings.

steel_grade_paper.note: Not in FEMM's library; see steel_grade.

current_angle_deg.quote: a constant current angle of θ = 90

coil_pitch_slots.figure: Fig. 6(a), p. 6: the authors' FE mesh of the PMVM as vector art (each triangle a filled path, read with femm_brain.vector_figure)

coil_pitch_slots.note: Each slot holds two coil sides stacked radially; the lower layer repeats the upper layer's phase one slot clockwise (Fig. 6(a), six slots: olive, olive/brown, brown, brown/green, green, green/yellow), so the coils span 5 of the 6 slots of a pole pitch, the go sides above (Table IV: overlapping).

copper_resistivity_ohm_m.reason: The paper states no conductor temperature for its FEA winding loss; copper's resistivity at 20 C (IEC 60028). The measured winding loss (570.2 W) exceeds the FEA's by 18.7%, copper's resistivity rise from 20 C to 68 C, a plausible test temperature; with the FEA at 75 C the test winding would have been at 136 C.
copper_resistivity_ohm_m.note: Pre-solve estimate: copper at 120 C (2.402e-8 ohm*m) lowers the current and torque by 15%.

copper_density_kg_per_m3.reason: Pure copper; the paper gives the copper mass, not its volume.
copper_density_kg_per_m3.note: Winding copper is quoted at 8890-8960; the current scales with the square root (0.4%).

magnet_br_T.reason: N48H's remanence is 1.37-1.43 T at 20 C (a grade's range); its middle. The paper names no magnet temperature for its FEA (its demagnetization check, Fig. 10, deems the machine safe below 80 C).
magnet_br_T.note: Brackets: 1.30 T (80 C at -0.12%/K) and 1.43 T; the pre-solve estimate moves the torque by -7.1% and +2.1%.

steel_grade.reason: M470-50A is not in FEMM's library; AISI M-43 is its usual equivalent (0.47 mm, 4.7 W/kg class). The library entry carries a 0.965 lamination fill; the rotor yoke is taken to be of the same laminations.

hub_mu_r.reason: The stator's support inside its 313 mm bore is not described; taken as non-magnetic.

band_margin_mm.reason: Thin air between the sliding band and each gap surface (a 0.5 mm band in the 1.5 mm gap).

tip_half_angle_deg.note: Half the tooth tip: the opening is sigma_so times the slot angle at the tip radius between the tooth sides extended.

shoe_root_radius_mm.note: Where the coils end (the slot closure).

tooth_strip_bottom_mm2.note: The part of a tooth's strip inside the slot-bottom circle.

slot_area_mm2.note: The coil region of one slot: the annular sector of a slot pitch between the slot bottom and the shoe roots less one tooth's strip.

current_density_rms_A_per_mm2.note: From P = rho J^2 V with V = m / density: 2.69 A/mm2 rms.

coil_side_peak_At.note: Peak ampere-turns of one coil side (half the slot's copper); the model's coil sides have one turn and carry this current.

metrics.name: torque_Nm
metrics.note: The rotor's torque, counterclockwise positive: FEMM's air-gap-element torque acts on the band's inner side (the stator here; design-dipole-torque-variant checks that sign), so the outer rotor's is its negative.

metrics.name: torque_block_Nm
metrics.note: Weighted stress tensor on the rotor's blocks (magnets and yoke), a cross-check.

assessors.quote: Predicted torque ripples of both PMVM and PMSM machines
assessors.note: The PMVM curve of Fig. 14, read from its filled outline (701 points) on the figure's gridlines (0-360 degrees at 50.27 pt per 90; 990-1040 N m at 16.60 pt per 10 N m): mean 1015.46 N m over the revolution, 1008.85-1021.49 N m. Its vertices lie about 3.55 degrees apart, so the curve samples the 198-per-revolution ripple at about 101 positions and aliases it (12 cycles drawn); a mean of such samples is still the average torque. Acceptance at 1%, the 2D FE rule; the digitization uncertainty, 0.2%, covers the line's width and the calibration. The torque's period at balanced currents is a sixth of an electrical period, 1.818 degrees (pole_pairs here is 6 pr, the sweep's span), so 12 positions over it average the whole waveform.

assessors.label: table
assessors.note: Table VII's FEA average torque, a comparator: 2.6% above the FE waveform it summarizes (Fig. 14); possibly the shaft torque including the core-loss torque (1015.46 + 476.4 W / 15.708 rad/s = 1045.8).

assessors.label: measured
assessors.note: Measured on the prototype, a comparator (3D, end effects, built tolerances).

assessors.location: Table VII, p. 8 and Fig. 14, p. 9 (vector art)
assessors.note: Fig. 14's peak to peak, 12.64 N m (Table VII's 1.25% of 1015.46 is 12.69): a comparator, since ripple is mesh noise on a symmetric machine and Fig. 14's samples alias it.

assessors.label: stress_tensor
assessors.quote: Predicted torque ripples of both PMVM and PMSM machines
assessors.note: The same target from the weighted stress tensor on the rotor's blocks, a cross-check of the band's torque.

1.66% of 1042.0 N m read as the cogging torque's peak: Fig. 13's measured PMVM cogging swings about +/-18 N m, which is Table VII's measured 1.80% of 1038.23 (18.7 N m) as a peak. A comparator (mesh noise; 12 positions over the 0.909 degree cogging period, 360/lcm(36, 66)).

assessors.label: measured
assessors.note: The measured 1.80% of 1038.23 N m, a comparator.

assessors.quote: Prediction from the construction: the winding's turns at the rotor's 33rd harmonic against the magnets' (the modulated 3rd harmonic has the same phase, eqs. (3)-(4)); balanced phases peaking in the order A, C, B as the rotor turns counterclockwise

assessors.label: flux_linkage
assessors.quote: Predicted torque ripples of both PMVM and PMSM machines
assessors.note: 3/2 pr (psi_d i_q - psi_q i_d) from the phase flux linkages and currents, averaged over the load positions: the lessons' check of a stress-tensor mean against the flux-linkage torque.

The 2D internal power factor (resistance and end-winding reactance neglected) at the load positions, a comparator: the paper's FEA adds an analytic end-winding inductance and the resistance (Section IV), which a 2D model lacks.

assessors.label: measured
assessors.quote: the PMVM achieves a power factor of 0.71
assessors.note: Measured at rated torque, a comparator.

controls.purpose: Every explicit element size and arc piece at 0.7 times.
The FEA winding loss at copper's 120 C resistivity (the hot end of the current gap): 15% less current.
The literal reading of Table III: 5 A/mm2 rms in the copper (the winding loss that current density gives at the frozen resistivity, density and copper mass, 1659.2 W).
The Metals Handbook DC curve of M-43, without a lamination fill, for the laminated library grade.
A magnetic stator support inside the bore.
Table V's 13.6 mm stator yoke, built inward from the slot bottoms (Di 311.88 instead of 313 mm).

The literal reading of sigma_so: 0.82 of the slot angle at the slot bottom (7.4 degrees) is 6.068 degrees of opening; expressed in the frozen reading's terms (of the slot angle at the tip radius, 7.7681 degrees), sigma_so = 0.7811.

coverage.reproduced: The PMVM's rated FE torque (acceptance), its winding sign and phase order against the construction; comparators for Table VII's FEA and measured torque, torque ripple, cogging torque and power factor.
coverage.not_reproduced: Losses, output power, efficiency, the power-factor and efficiency curves (Figs. 17-18), open-circuit voltage (the turns are not given), demagnetization (Fig. 10), the optimization study (Figs. 4-9) and the PMSM.
